ATmega328P. Seen from above, the USB socket and the power jack on the left. The gaps between the headers are drawn roughly.
Renesas RA4M1, the R3\'s headers at 5 V. Its own: a DAC on A0, an op-amp on A1–A3, CAN on D4 and D5 (with a transceiver), Serial1 on D0 and D1 (Serial is the USB). Seen as the R3.
ATmega32U4, the Uno\'s headers. I²C is on D2 and D3, Serial1 on D0 and D1 (Serial is the USB); SPI only on the 6-pin ICSP header. Seen as the Uno.
ATmega2560. Seen from above, the USB socket and the power jack on the left, the double header along the right edge (its even pins inside). PWM on D2–D13 and D44–D46. The gaps are drawn roughly.
ATmega328P. Seen from above, USB at the top. The pins are numbered around the board, from TX (1).
ATmega4809, the Nano\'s pins at 5 V. Every digital pin takes an interrupt; A6 and A7 work as digital pins too. Seen as the Nano.
The Nano\'s pins, but at 3.3 V: 5 V on them damages the board. I²C on A4 and A5. Seen as the Nano.
ATmega328P, at 5 V (16 MHz) or 3.3 V (8 MHz). Seen from above, the programming (FTDI) header at the top. A4–A7 are pads inside the board, placed roughly here: they differ between makers.
